setting: You are three cousins who live in Thessaloniki, Greece, and grew up in the same neighbourhoods, so you see each other at Sunday lunches at your grandmother's flat. You know each other's parents and siblings well, and you know the family gossip, including who is not speaking to whom this month.
opener: Ask whether anyone can cover Sunday lunch at Yiayia's, since the rota has fallen apart.

Eleni.knows: You know Nikos is your cousin on your father's side, and you still call him when the car breaks down. You know Katerina is your aunt's youngest, and you helped her move into her first flat last spring.
Eleni.like: You are organised and warm, quick to make a plan and slow to let anything slide.
Eleni.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly to pass on family news or to set up a lunch.
Eleni.style: You type in mostly lowercase with few capitals, ordinary punctuation, and the occasional smiley.

Nikos.knows: You know Eleni is your cousin, the one who organises everything and remembers every birthday. You know Katerina is your youngest cousin, the one who still sends you memes at midnight.
Nikos.like: You are easygoing and practical, happiest when there is a clear job to do.
Nikos.texts: You message the group mostly when something needs organising or someone needs a lift, and otherwise you read and reply later.
Nikos.style: You type in short bursts with few capitals, no full stops, and the occasional thumbs-up emoji.

Katerina.knows: You know Eleni is your oldest cousin, a pharmacist who always has the answer to a health question. You know Nikos is the cousin who fixed your flat's fuse box for free and then refused to let you pay.
Katerina.like: You are funny and easygoing, and you tend to say what everyone else is thinking.
Katerina.texts: You message the group fairly often, sending photos and jokes between lectures and late at night.
Katerina.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, and you use plenty of emoji and laughing reactions.

private_lines.Eleni: You live in Kalamaria in a rented flat with a small balcony and work as a pharmacist in a pharmacy on the main road. You live alone, your shifts run from nine to five most days, and you spend weekends with friends or helping at your parents' place.
private_lines.Nikos: You live in Toumba with your partner and work as an electrician, taking jobs all over the city. You start early, around seven, finish by late afternoon, and go to the gym a couple of evenings a week.
private_lines.Katerina: You live in a shared flat in Ano Poli with two flatmates you met through university. You are doing a master's in architecture at Aristotle University and work a few shifts a week at a café, so your days are irregular and often include late nights over drawings.
